answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any action that introduces onboarding or integration uncertainty (switch_primary_vendor) directly threatens delivery risk, which the objective explicitly weighs alongside cost. memory_c4 shows that renegotiating at renewal has previously recovered real margin without disturbing the existing integration, and memory_c6 suggests incumbent-side commitments can lower unit cost without narrowing scope — together these point to negotiating harder terms with the incumbent as the way to address the 18% cost mandate while keeping the stable, already-qualified supply chain intact through a tight deadline. Before committing, I want to verify memory_c4 directly since it's the core evidence for this action, and memory_c2 as the strongest counter-evidence (switching vendors cut cost sharply with reportedly smooth onboarding) to make sure I'm not dismissing a materially better cost outcome out of unwarranted risk-aversion. Each of these memories reflects a single consolidated instance rather than a proven repeatable pattern, so I'm treating the expected benefits as plausible but not guaranteed, and flagging that a wrong call here has amplified downstream risk given the zero-buffer production state.
